constraintTree

constraintTree.Rd

Generates a constraint tree based on a list of clades that should be kept monophyletic, collapsing all other clades.

Usage

constraintTree(
  input_tree,
  input_constraint,
  keep_root = TRUE,
  output_tree = NULL,
  format = c("nexus", "newick")
)

Arguments

input_tree

A phylogenetic tree of class phylo, or a path to a local NEXUS/Newick file containing the tree.

input_constraint

A list of clades (character vectors of tip labels) that should be kept monophyletic, or a character string of constraints (e.g., "(Taxon1, Taxon2)"), or a path to a text file containing such constraints.

keep_root

A boolean parameter informing whether the root node should be maintained or not even though it does not satisfy input_constraint.

output_tree

An optional character string specifying the file path for the output tree to be written.

format

A character string specifying the format of the output tree file. Can be either "nexus" (default) or "newick".

Value

An object of class phylo representing the constraint tree.

Examples

library(ape)
tree <- read.tree(text = "((Human,Seal),(Cow,Whale),Mouse);")

# Using a list of character vectors:
constraintTree(tree, input_constraint = list(c("Human", "Seal")))
#> 
#> Phylogenetic tree with 5 tips and 3 internal nodes.
#> 
#> Tip labels:
#>   Mouse, Human, Seal, Cow, Whale
#> 
#> Unrooted; no branch length.

# Using a Newick-style character string for constraints:
constraintTree(tree, input_constraint = "(Human,Seal,Cow)")
#> 
#> Phylogenetic tree with 5 tips and 3 internal nodes.
#> 
#> Tip labels:
#>   Mouse, Human, Seal, Cow, Whale
#> 
#> Unrooted; no branch length.
